reason: E1 directly supports that cold spray retains the BCC structure and that thermal spray causes phase changes and in-flight oxidation, but it also states that oxides from in-flight oxidation improve hardness and wear, contradicting the premise that minimizing oxidation improves mechanical properties. E2 shows cold-sprayed coatings can achieve higher hardness after heat treatment, but does not address in-flight oxidation or phase stability during deposition.
premises: Cold spray retains the as-atomized BCC phase of HEA powders, unlike thermal spray which can cause phase changes.
Cold spray minimizes in-flight oxidation compared to thermal spray processes.
Minimizing in-flight oxidation and phase changes leads to a more homogeneous, stable, and adherent bond coat.
Reduced oxidation and phase stability improve mechanical integrity (hardness, wear resistance) and durability.
